title: Pathwell Harada Chart (excerpt)
lede: The center is what the story is saying. The eight around any box are how the story gets there, and each of those opens into its own eight, as deep as it needs. Select a box to read it; select it again, or use Open, to make it the center.
footer: An excerpt of the Pathwell chart, for learning the method: the center, one actor opened through its eight facets, and one story engine with a problem broken into options. Quotes check against Story/Chapters in the Pathwell repository.

root.title: Choose your own life, ready or not, and let other people choose theirs
root.note: The last page says it with the first page's words. In Chapter 1 he asks “Ready?”, she says “No,” and he says “Perfect” and takes her hand. In Chapter 18 she asks, he says “No,” and she says “Perfect,” and he comes because she asked and he said yes. Same words. What changed is who is choosing. (Thesis: control is not competence, and Elizabeth matters without any power source.)

kids.title: Elizabeth: the one who learns to choose
kids.note: She starts the book handing things over before she's decided to. She ends it choosing where they go and asking him along. She never gets magic; her choices count because they're only human.

kids.title: Start: she hands things over before she's decided to
kids.note: The book has to start with someone who lets other people choose for her, or there's nothing to climb. The character bible calls it compliance under pressure.

kids.title: Three weeks in, nothing unpacked
kids.quote: Three weeks. Twenty-one days of unpacked boxes and takeout trying to figure out what came next.
kids.note: A new life she hasn't moved into yet.

kids.title: She left because staying felt worse
kids.quote: A life she'd packed into garbage bags and moved across the city because staying felt worse than leaving, but leaving didn't feel like anything at all.
kids.note: Her real problem, said once, in her own breakdown.

kids.title: Nobody at work has noticed her
kids.quote: He'd laughed at her joke about the landlord, which was more than anyone from work had managed.
kids.note: The stranger going through her boxes is the one person at her party who laughed.

kids.title: Wants: her books back, then the truth
kids.note: What she's after changes as she climbs. Each want is a little more her own than the one before.

kids.title: Nana's cookbook back
kids.quote: He still has it.
kids.note: Ch2–3. Property, not trust.

kids.title: Answers before she goes anywhere
kids.quote: I'm not going anywhere without getting some questions answered.

kids.title: To know why it came to her door
kids.quote: She wanted to know why something impossible had come through her door before the magic went wrong.
kids.note: The first want that isn't about getting something back.

kids.title: Needs: to choose for herself, even when nobody asks
kids.note: Her need is self-direction. Nobody hands it to her; she takes it one rung at a time (Writing Principles 7).

kids.title: Nobody is going to make her important
kids.quote: Then you were never the point.
kids.note: The diner takes away the importance Pathwell gave her by mistake.

kids.title: She has to make herself the driver
kids.quote: Elizabeth chose the ditch.

kids.title: She has to say no and mean it
kids.quote: I don't need to be rescued.

kids.title: Stands for: mattering without power
kids.note: The thesis: her choices matter because they're human. If she ever casts, the book becomes an empowerment fantasy (Thesis, critical constraint).

kids.title: She never does magic
kids.note: Canon hard boundary. She can own, carry, give, or position charged things. She can't use them.

kids.title: Ordinary people feel the magic too
kids.quote: None of that had been hers, and she held on to that.
kids.note: Her overwhelm in the Space Between isn't a hidden gift.

kids.title: The dagger is Stansbury's magic, her choice
kids.quote: Elizabeth already had the dagger in her hand.

kids.title: In her way: people who choose for her, and her habit of letting them
kids.note: Her obstacle is outside and inside at once: people who decide for her, and her habit of letting them.

kids.title: He decides the danger is hers
kids.quote: Your house has now been marked, magically speaking.

kids.title: He offers a choice while holding her things
kids.quote: The choice is yours, Lizzy.

kids.title: He answers for her
kids.quote: Pathwell answered for her. "No."

kids.title: Arc: pulled, pushing, choosing
kids.note: Eight rungs. Each one is something she does, not a door someone opens for her. The ninth rung is the last page.

kids.title: She follows him for her books
kids.quote: He still has it.
kids.note: Rung 1: she stops absorbing what happened and goes after something that's hers.

kids.title: He tells her it's her choice
kids.quote: The choice is yours, Lizzy.
kids.note: He's holding her books while he says it.

kids.title: He leaves her alone in the neon
kids.quote: She watched him walk off, leaving her in the red neon glow.

kids.title: Nana's name brings the warmth back
kids.quote: Then a warmth, the taste of butter and sugar
kids.note: R21: the echo of Nana's voice through the page.

kids.title: She looks for the books and they're gone
kids.quote: Her eyes swept the table, slowly at first. Then darting.

kids.title: She runs after him
kids.quote: He still has it.

kids.title: She steps through for the books, not for him
kids.quote: He still had her books.

kids.title: She chooses the forest over the sidewalk
kids.quote: She had put them there herself, after the shopkeeper had offered to send her back to the sidewalk.
kids.note: Rung 2: the first choice she makes with her books back in her hands (R31).

kids.title: The shop gives her books back, not him
kids.quote: These were never his to spend.

kids.title: She's offered a way home
kids.quote: after the shopkeeper had offered to send her back to the sidewalk.

kids.title: She puts her books on his cart herself
kids.quote: She had put them there herself

kids.title: It still feels strange to her
kids.quote: That fact still felt strange enough to keep checking.

kids.title: She goes on for her own question
kids.quote: Not because he had her things. He didn't.

kids.title: She remembers it at the end
kids.quote: had chosen a forest without knowing what it was.

kids.title: Voice: sincere, not witty; her body knows first
kids.note: Character bible: her jokes are small and defensive; physical sensation comes before named feeling.

kids.title: She worries about ordinary things under pressure
kids.quote: I have to get my dry cleaning before the meeting.

kids.title: She takes the literal question
kids.quote: It's Thursday.

kids.title: She snaps when she has to
kids.quote: "No," she snapped.

kids.title: End: she asks, and lets the answer be no
kids.note: Who she's become: she decides where they go and asks him along, without pardoning him.

kids.title: She won't make his guilt her job
kids.quote: I need you not to make me responsible for whether you become a better person.

kids.title: She doesn't know if she forgives him
kids.quote: I don't know if I forgive you.

kids.title: Her ordinary life is still hers
kids.quote: It was still hers.
kids.note: The spoon. The apartment, the job, the plant.

kids.title: She was never the point
kids.note: Pathwell made her important by misreading a danger that was his. The book takes that importance away so she can earn the other kind: mattering because of what she does, not because something came for her.

kids.title: Something was at her door before any magic
kids.quote: Something wet and dark sagged into the gap.
kids.note: The fair-play clue, in Chapter 1.

kids.title: She sees it through the chain
kids.quote: Something wet and dark sagged into the gap.

kids.title: He calls it housekeeping
kids.quote: Just cleaning up a mess.
kids.note: Literally true.

kids.title: He decides it's after her, and tells her so
kids.quote: Your house has now been marked, magically speaking.
kids.note: A half-bluff (R27).

kids.title: He thought she'd know
kids.quote: You really don't know?

kids.title: He checks the hall and goes still
kids.quote: Sticking his head out, he checked up and down the hall. Then he went still.

kids.title: Why he was really there
kids.quote: He'd been at the party, talking to everybody.
kids.note: Nobody asks, all book. P66's central finding.

kids.title: The evidence is all on the page
kids.note: Every piece of the answer is there. Nothing connects them.

kids.title: He was at her party
kids.quote: He'd been at the party, talking to everybody.

kids.title: He looked at old notebooks
kids.quote: She'd seen him peering into an open box of old notebooks once
kids.note: R48's clue.

kids.title: He stayed after everyone left
kids.quote: She'd thought he'd left with the rest.

kids.title: He read her diary
kids.quote: reading her diary like a magazine in a waiting room.

kids.title: The shop trades in people's lives
kids.quote: Not books — lives.

kids.title: He owes the shop
kids.quote: You already owe quite a bit.

kids.title: Her books were his stock
kids.quote: He brought outside property into an open transaction

kids.title: Camp calls him a thief
kids.quote: I was only ever no good at being a thief.

kids.title: Fix 1: she asks him in Chapter 1
kids.note: The author's line: “What are you still doing here?” The reply has to change with it.

kids.title: Now: “Do you mind?” / “Not at all”
kids.quote: "Not at all," he said, and turned a page.

kids.title: B0: he just turns a page
kids.note: Recommended. Her question doesn't get his attention. The thud does.
kids.proposed: "What are you still doing here?" / He turned a page.

kids.title: C0: “Reading,”
kids.note: Funnier, but a new Pathwell joke and another dodge.
kids.proposed: "What are you still doing here?" / "Reading," he said, and turned a page.

kids.title: Fix 2: she works it out at the counter
kids.note: B1. Her suspicion, not his confession. It goes right after the ledger line, and the shopkeeper's “These were never his to spend.” confirms it.
kids.proposed: Elizabeth thought of Pathwell on her living-room floor, turning the pages of her diary like he was pricing it.

kids.title: Camp sees the first part doesn't fit
kids.quote: The first part did not.
kids.note: The question becomes hers.

kids.title: Mama Baga asks the timing
kids.quote: It was already at the door before you used the cookbook?

kids.title: After the working, it ate the waste
kids.quote: It changed targets. Fresh waste.
